summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was readmitted two days after discharge for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and hematemesis. Evaluation revealed stable cirrhosis without decompensation, no active variceal bleeding, and a stable hemoglobin level. Imaging showed small bowel malrotation without obstruction, which may contribute to his chronic gastrointestinal symptoms. He was managed conservatively with a soft diet, metoclopramide for gastric motility, and ondansetron for nausea. Elevated tTG-IgA and total IgA levels suggest possible celiac disease, warranting outpatient evaluation. He remained hemodynamically stable, and his symptoms improved. He was discharged home with continued home medications, new prescriptions for metoclopramide and ondansetron, and follow-up plans with the transplant clinic for nutrition consultation, CBC monitoring, and further workup of celiac disease.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
